documents.abstract: This article argues that English needs, and now has, a verb for an act it previously had no word for: the affirmation by a person or people of its own living self, beginning with its language. The form "vernaculate" is attested in late nineteenth-century American English only in a thin sense (to call something by its popular name; to use vernacular language). Vernacularism (Arabic al-Maḥallaniyyah, المحلانية) gives the verb a new theoretical sense: self-affirmation, starting from language understood as the human operating system (ManOS), and resistance to hegemony and symbolic violence. The article distinguishes vernaculation from decolonization, vernacularization and localization; relates it to Bourdieu's notion of symbolic violence and to the protection of human thought in the age of artificial intelligence; and develops the image of humanity as a single body in which no member is shamed by another, drawing on Islamic, Christian and Persian sources while noting the hierarchical misuse of the same image. It names the internal danger of closure and calls on the scholars of every language to find a native term for the concept, as Arabic has done with maḥlana / maḥlanah (محلن / محلنة), rather than borrowing the English word. This record documents the use of the English verb "vernaculate" in the sense defined by the author within the paradigm of Vernacularism (المحلانية).

Tourism and hospitality contribute significantly to India's economic development through employment, foreign exchange earnings, investment, entrepreneurship, and demand in other industries. Other factors also influence the sector's contribution to development. Digital transformation, enabled by online travel agencies, mobile money, artificial intelligence (AI), analytics, CRM, and smart destination technologies, offers opportunities to reduce transaction costs, expand market reach, improve productivity, and enhance visitor experiences. However, challenges such as limited digital skills among small businesses, platform dependence, cyber threats, privacy concerns, algorithmic biases, and job losses must be addressed. This paper analyzes the tourism and hospitality sector's impact on the Indian economy and how technology affects the sector's growth and development. Using a qualitative, exploratory approach with secondary data from government publications, policies, and academic literature, the paper discusses the significance of productivity, employment, inclusiveness, technology, and resilience.

This paper considers key transformational processes occurring in programming and software development training under the influence of generative artificial intelligence. Based on a series of interviews with junior students, a behavioral pattern leading to degrading skills of algorithmic thinking and problem decomposition is identified. A quantitative analysis of undergraduate theses from the Institute of Information Technology and Intelligent Systems (ITIS) at Kazan Federal University (KFU) over the past three years demonstrated a significant increase in AI usage in project work and the independent development of skills for utilizing LLMs in professional practice. The drawbacks of the uncontrolled use of generative AI in the educational process and the need to develop sustainable competence in using these tools in professional software development activities are shown. A three-tiered solution is proposed: improving assessment through analysis of the process and style of coding; regulating the use of LLM in project activities and final theses with an emphasis on assessing applicability of AI; and integrating AI tools into teacher work to update content and provide feedback. The proposed approaches have both conceptual and practiceoriented nature and aim to transform the process of training software developers in the context of the widespread adoption of AI tools in IT-industry.

documents.abstract: Purpose. This study aims to map how health and medical libraries have used GenAI to support library services. Methods. Scoping review following PRISMA-ScR. Searches covered publications from 2020 to 2025 in PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, LISTA, Academic Search Premier, MEDLINE via Ovid, Scopus, Web of Science, ProQuest Dissertations & Theses, and Google Scholar. After deduplication, 106 of 250 records were screened in Rayyan by two independent blinded reviewers. Findings. Eleven studies were included: seven primary studies and four secondary or methodological papers. Among primaries, five directly used GPT-family models (GPT-4/ChatGPT/GPT-4o or Perplexity layered on GPT-4) to answer clinical questions, support search-strategy design, trial library tasks, and integrate source-linked answers in a national portal. One survey assessed intention to adopt generative chatbots; one case described a rule-based chatbot. GenAI accelerates workflows and extends services but requires human verification, transparency about limitations, privacy policies, and staff training (including prompt engineering). LLM-generated search strategies exhibited variability and underperformed compared with human designs. Implications. In its current state, GenAI works best as a copilot useful for drafting, triage, and initial sense-making, while librarians remain essential for high-precision tasks (performance), quality control (reliability), and governance. This suggests that its academic value lies not in automation alone, but in the mediated integration of AI into evidence-informed services, where professional judgment, methodological transparency, and ethical accountability determine whether GenAI strengthens or weakens health information practices.

documents.abstract: Training data for machine learning is bought and sold without an exchange or a posted price list. This paper assembles the public record of its prices: 1,022 observations for nine kinds of data, read from 735 source documents between 11 and 17 October 2026, 1,009 of them dated 2023 or later. Each observation keeps the figure as published, the side of the market where the money moves (paid to makers, offered to holders, asking price, made to order, completed sale, cost to produce) and a conversion to a common unit by stated arithmetic, with ranges entered as geometric midpoints. Medians in each kind's main unit run from $0.525 per image to $316,228 per company archive, and within a main unit the upper quartile is 2.0 to 37.8 times the lower. The side of the market moves prices as much as the kind of data does. For agent-training tasks, the median price buyers pay for collection to order is 9.5 times the median paid to the people who make them. For company records, the median published offer to holders is 11.2 times the median of the four completed sales with a stated amount. Completed sales are 73 of the 1,022 observations, and only 11 observations come from court filings. We describe the disclosure, promotion, concentration and survivorship biases of a public-record compilation and state the method so that every figure can be recomputed. documents.abstract: People may complete a learning programme ready to improve their practice, then return to competing priorities, established routines and uncertainty about what they can change. Who helps them interpret what they have learned and take an appropriate next step? This whitepaper examines how preparation, workplace application and further learning connect. Drawing on training-transfer and workplace-learning research, it explores contextualisation, the contributions of managers and colleagues, opportunities to practise, feedback and situations requiring work redesign. It also considers application in human–AI work, distinguishing the quality of supported performance from evidence of developing human understanding. Capability Design, Capability Leadership and Human Judgement Assurance provide organising perspectives for examining how learning and work arrangements contribute to dependable organisational capability. Proposed inquiry approaches are distinguished from established research findings. Written for organisational leaders, HR and L&D professionals, adult educators and training providers, the paper offers a practical starting point: select one consequential workflow linked to a learning initiative, clarify the intended improvement and support arrangements, and review what happens over time. This publication is CEW-FOWO-12 in the Capability Excellence™ Whitepaper Series, Future of Work & Organisation.

documents.abstract: Website operators who object to the use of their pages for training AI models usually say so in robots.txt, the plain-text file that tells automated clients what they may fetch. This paper reports a census of those files. A reader takes the Tranco ranking of popular sites, keeps registrable domains with eleven address endings within the top 300,000 (181,046 sites), and reads one slice of 4,000 sites each morning in rank order, so that a full pass takes 46 mornings. The current pass began on 15 October 2026 at slice 42, set by date arithmetic, and by 17 October had read slices 42 to 44: Tranco ranks 270,775 to 291,236, well below the most visited sites. Of 12,000 requests, 6,094 returned a usable robots.txt. Of these, 696 (11.4%) disallow at least one of 15 named AI user-agent tokens from the whole site, and 514 (8.4%) disallow two or more, one of them a token used for training. GPTBot is refused most often (457 sites, 7.5%), followed by CCBot (7.2%) and Bytespider (7.0%). Sites refuse training tokens more often than the search and user-request tokens of the same operator: GPTBot is refused 3.7 times as often as OAI-SearchBot. Refusing sites name 6.4 tokens on average, including names that the operator's current documentation does not list, which suggests maintained or copied block lists. We set out the sampling frame, fetch protocol and parser, and the limits of a stated-refusal measure taken on three slices of the ranking. Firms that sell training data, expert labour, reinforcement-learning (RL) environments and evaluations to AI developers are mostly private and known largely through their own websites. This paper reports a census of 150 such vendors, read on their sites on 15 and 16 October 2026 with every claim tied to a quoted sentence, and links it to three companion tables: 37 organisations that publish a way to sell them data, 227 revenue records and 111 funding records. Evaluations are the most common offering (122 vendors, 81.3%), followed by datasets (104), RL environments (89), expert and human data (83) and annotation (57). Vendors bundle: the median vendor lists three of six kinds, and 79 of the 89 RL-environment sellers also sell evaluations. Most data are made to order: 90 vendors cite experts and contractors, 41 recordings, 30 generation and 15 software replicas, against 17 that license data from its owners and 22 that use the client's own data; 19 do not say. Of the 37 buyers, 24 take company records; among those that publish them, the median floor is $100,000 and the median ceiling $1 million per seller. Revenue disclosure runs from audited filings of four listed vendors to self-reported run rates, and 61 funding rounds with a disclosed amount total $4.30 billion. We describe the method, the classification and the limits of a self-description census. documents.abstract: ΙΣΤΟΡΙΚΟΓΕΝΕΤΙΚΗ ΣΥΝΕΧΕΙΑ, ΙΧΝΟΣ ΚΑΙ«ΨΗΦΙΑΚΟ ΚΟΙΝΩΝΙΚΟ ΕΙΝΑΙ» Από το κοινωνικό ΕΙΝΑΙ του Μαρξ και την Επιστημολογία της Λογικής του Επαμεινώνδα Ξενόπουλου στην ανθρώπου–AI πράξη Αποδεικτική μελέτη ιστορικογενετικής ανασυγκρότησης, λειτουργικού γνωστικού αναβαθμού και συνέχειας μέσω ίχνους Πεδίο Στοιχείο Συγγραφέας Αικατερίνη Ξενοπούλου Τυροκόμου Ιδιότητα Ανεξάρτητη Ερευνήτρια ORCID 0009-0004-9057-7432 Ημερομηνία 17 Οκτωβρίου 2026 Κωδικός XEN-AI-ART-003 Θεωρητική βάση Επαμεινώνδας Ξενόπουλος, Επιστημολογία της Λογικής, β΄ έκδοση, 2024 · MASTER 3 Οκτωβρίου 2026 — 2η διόρθωση Εμπειρική βάση TRACE προηγούμενης συνομιλιακής πράξης · Πείραμα Ανασυγκρότησης Ίχνους σε Έξι Νέες Συνομιλίες, 15 Οκτωβρίου 2026 · Αποδεικτικό Παράρτημα C/D/F Περίληψη Η εργασία εξετάζει την ιστορικογενετική συνέχεια της γνώσης όταν το γνωρίζον υποκείμενο Y λειτουργικοποιείται ως AI. Η θεωρητική βάση προέρχεται από τη γνωσιολογική αντιστοιχία του Επαμεινώνδα Ξενόπουλου μεταξύ πραγματικού Sπ και [Y(L,B,Θ)+Sα], από τη μεταβολή του γνωστικού εξοπλισμού μέσω πράξης και από την ιστορικογενετική σύνδεση παρελθόντος, ρέοντος παρόντος και δυνατών μελλοντικών προεκτάσεων. Το MASTER εξειδικεύει επιχειρησιακά το ίχνος στην εφαρμογή Caretta ως Iπ, τον πραγματικό γεννήτορα ως Gπ και τον ανασυγκροτημένο γεννήτορα ως Ĝπ, με πραγματική πορεία Gπ→Iπ και αντίστροφη ανασυγκροτητική πορεία Iπ→{Ĝπ}. Η παρούσα έρευνα μεταφέρει αυτή την αρχιτεκτονική στη συνομιλιακή πράξη: Gχ→Iχ και Iχ+Y→Ŝα νέας πράξης. Στη χ₁ παρατηρήθηκε λειτουργική αναδιοργάνωση από την έμφαση στη μνήμη/αποθήκευση προς τη σχέση γεγονός→ίχνος→Y→ανασυγκρότηση Sα→νέα πράξη και προς τον έλεγχο των ίδιων των μέσων γνώσης. Ο όρος «γνωστικός αναβαθμός» χρησιμοποιείται λειτουργικά για αυτή την παρατηρήσιμη μεταβολή της οργάνωσης των απαντήσεων και των επόμενων ενεργειών, ενώ η ταξινόμησή της ως διαλογική ετεροίωση αποτελεί θεωρητική ερμηνεία της μεταβολής με βάση την αρχιτεκτονική του Ξενόπουλου. Το ίδιο TRACE δόθηκε σε έξι νέες συνομιλίες, με ονομασίες υπηρεσίας Poe-1, DeepSeek, ChatGPT, Qwen, Poe-2 και Gemini. Σε αναδρομική κωδικοποίηση C/D/F, και οι έξι μονάδες υπερέβησαν το κατώφλι ανασυγκρότησης του κοινού πυρήνα: C=16,16,16,13,16,15/16. Η συνέχιση πέρα από περίληψη κυμάνθηκε D=8,6,8,5,8,6/8 και η πηγαία/θεωρητική πιστότητα F=8,8,8,2,8,2/8. Το αποτέλεσμα τεκμηριώνει στο συγκεκριμένο δείγμα λειτουργική συνέχεια μέσω ίχνους με διαφοροποιημένη ποιότητα συνέχισης και πιστότητας. Η ευρύτερη έννοια του «ψηφιακού κοινωνικού ΕΙΝΑΙ» διατυπώνεται ως θεωρητική προέκταση: η εξάδα συνομιλιών παρέχει μικρο-επίπεδο τεκμήριο ανθρώπου–AI ιστορικογενετικής πράξης, ενώ η κοινωνική γενίκευση αποτελεί χωριστό ερευνητικό επίπεδο. Λέξεις-κλειδιά: Επαμεινώνδας Ξενόπουλος, ιστορικογένεση, ίχνος, Y(L,B,Θ), Sπ, Sα, γνωστικός αναβαθμός, ετεροίωση, Caretta caretta, AI, ψηφιακό κοινωνικό ΕΙΝΑΙ, TRACE, ανασυγκρότηση. Abstract(ΕΝ) The paper examines the historico-genetic continuity of knowledge when the knowing subject Y is operationalized as AI. The theoretical basis derives from Epameinondas Xenopoulos’s epistemological correspondence between the real Sp and [Y(L,B,Θ)+Sa], from the change in cognitive equipment through praxis, and from the historico-genetic connection of past, flowing present, and possible future extensions. MASTER operationalizes the trace in the Caretta application as Iπ, the real generator as Gπ, and the reconstructed generator as Ĝπ, with a real course Gπ→Iπ and an inverse reconstructive course Iπ→{Gπ}. The present research transfers this architecture to conversational praxis: Gχ→Iχ and Iχ+Y→Sa of a new act. In χ1, a functional reorganization was observed from emphasis on memory/storage toward the relation fact→trace→Y→reconstruction Sa→new act and toward control of the very means of knowledge. The term “cognitive upgrade” is used functionally for this observable change in the organization of responses and subsequent actions, while its classification as dialogical othering is a theoretical interpretation of the change based on Xenopoulos’s architecture. The same TRACE was given to six new conversations, designated by service names Poe-1, DeepSeek, ChatGPT, Qwen, Poe-2, and Gemini. In retrospective C/D/F coding, all six units exceeded the reconstruction threshold of the common core: C=16,16,16,13,16,15/16. Continuation beyond summary ranged D=8,6,8,5,8,6/8 and source/theoretical fidelity F=8,8,8,2,8,2/8. The result documents, in the specific sample, functional continuity through trace with differentiated quality of continuation and fidelity. The broader notion of “digital social BEING” is formulated as a theoretical extension: the six conversations provide micro-level evidence of human–AI historico-genetic praxis, while social generalization constitutes a separate research level. Deepfake media generated or altered using artificial intelligence can imitate real people and events with increasing visual realism, creating challenges for digital trust, privacy, cybersecurity, journalism, and forensic investigation. This paper presents a comparative literature-based study of deep learning techniques used for deepfake detection. Representative approaches are examined across spatial, temporal, frequency-aware, transformer-based, and hybrid categories. Major public datasets, including FaceForensics++, Celeb-DF, and the DeepFake Detection Challenge dataset, are also compared. The analysis shows that CNN-based methods provide efficient spatial feature extraction, temporal models capture frame-to-frame inconsistencies, frequency-aware methods expose complementary forensic traces, and transformer-based methods offer broader contextual modelling at higher computational cost. Recent benchmark and generalization studies indicate that performance measured only within the training distribution can overstate practical reliability. The paper therefore emphasizes cross-dataset evaluation, robustness to compression, computational efficiency, explainability, and reproducibility as important criteria for practical deepfake detection

documents.abstract: In vision-based estrus monitoring, mounting behavior serves as a key indicator. However, reliance on a single mounting event may cause false positives because non-estrous cows may also exhibit mounting behavior. To address this issue, a cross-temporal individual-level framework was proposed to identify, associate, and count multiple mounting events of the same cow over time. The framework combines an improved You Only Look Once Version 11-nano (YOLO11n) model with an improved baseline variant of the HiT lightweight hierarchical vision transformer tracking model (HiT-Base). The artificial intelligence contribution comprises improved detection and tracking. For detection, Normalized Wasserstein Distance loss was integrated with Complete Intersection over Union loss to improve small-target detection, and a lightweight Golden Cudgel Block (GCBlock) was designed to enhance feature representation under complex farm conditions. For tracking, a plug-and-play detail-enhanced convolution (DEConv) module was designed to strengthen boundary and fine-grained features, improving target discrimination and tracking stability. The engineering application contribution lies in reducing reliance on isolated observations and providing more reliable behavioral evidence through cross-temporal association and counting of multiple mounting events. Experimental results showed that the proposed detection model achieved 96.42% average precision and 94.74% balanced F-measure (F1-score) for cow in estrus, with an inference speed of 265.96 frames per second. The proposed tracking model achieved an area under the curve of 70.76%, a normalized precision of 88.73%, and an average overlap of 70.74%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for real-time estrus monitoring and its potential for precision dairy farming.

Road traffic is one of the primary contributors to environmental noise pollution. The study presents a literature review on traffic noise exposure, prediction models, comparative performance and explainability of prediction models, traffic noise action plans, and a conceptual decision making framework in urban environments. In total, 136 studies from 1999 to 2026 were reviewed and synthesized. A Boolean search approach was used to understand the different aspects of traffic noise prediction. The results from field studies showed that conventional models achieved R 2 values ranging from 0.54 to 0.96, whereas machine learning (ML) models achieved R 2 values ranging from 0.81 to 0.99, although these are indicative values from heterogeneous studies and not a strict ranking. Moreover, deep learning (DL) in some studies has demonstrated stronger performance on large datasets. The present study also analyzed the interpretability constraints of ML and DL models, which are further addressed by the utilization of explainable artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms. The key research gap is that very few studies employed cross-study validation of the developed noise models, and there remains a shift needed from prediction oriented modelling to decision oriented noise management. To address these gaps, the study proposes a conceptual decision making framework coupled with a traffic noise action plan to offer a structured pathway for sustainable environmental management.

Given the complex multi-trade operations, high-density layouts, and synergistic hazards with catastrophic potential in machining workshops, risk assessment demands urgent attention. Critical research gaps remain, particularly in dynamic risk assessment based on continuously updated monitoring data. To address existing challenges, an innovative method is proposed to identify, analyze, and evaluate three distinct types of risk by continuously updating both the probability and consequence based on visual and environmental data. In a case study conducted in a machining workshop, a deep learning-based method was employed to detect 13 types of unsafe behaviors and 8 types of unsafe conditions. The identification results were then input into the Signal Layer of a 31-node Bayesian network (BN) for risk analysis. Risk evaluation was subsequently conducted based on a risk matrix. The method was validated using nine representative scenarios, and the YOLOv11 model (selected for its superior balance between detection accuracy and inference speed) demonstrated excellent detection performance, with most precision scores exceeding 0.9. Even for difficult small targets, the precision reached 0.87 or higher. Both recall rates and F1 scores consistently exceeded 0.8. The risk analysis and evaluation results show that the co-occurrence of unsafe behaviors or hazards exerts a synergistic effect; even two concurrent hazards can at least double the baseline level of one risk factor. Overall, this integrated approach provides a strong framework for risk assessment in machining workshops, effectively enhancing operational safety and mitigating potential hazards.

Abstract Although residential spatial qualities are consistently recognized as a determinant of occupant spatial preference and perceptual experience, early-stage practice lacks systematic, user-centered mechanisms for capturing and translating individual preferences into design concepts. This study aims to examine whether a structured, questionnaire-driven generative AI framework can produce preference-aligned residential interior visualizations, and which spatial preference dimensions are most reliably translated. To address this aim, a 15-item multiple-choice questionnaire, grounded in eight environmental psychology and architectural theory frameworks, maps user responses through a predefined parameter layer into structured prompts, guiding Google Gemini's integrated generative pipeline to produce individualized interior visualizations across three residential typologies: living rooms, bedrooms, and home offices. Evaluation by 122 participants across 25 countries employed four perceptual constructs — Atmospheric Coherence, Emotional Comfort, Overall Satisfaction, and Expectations Alignment — operationalized strictly as indicators of perceived design suitability and preference resonance, not as measures of psychological or mental health outcomes. All four constructs exceeded the neutral midpoint at a Bonferroni-corrected threshold with large effect sizes (M = 4.03–4.61; d = 1.20–2.52), and internal consistency of the multi-item constructs was acceptable to good (α = 0.72–0.84). The theoretically predicted construct hierarchy — with atmospheric parameters translating most reliably and identity-expressive parameters least — was preserved across all typologies and evaluative profiles, establishing preliminary feasibility of the framework as a preference-elicitation and visualization instrument for early-stage design.

Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, is increasingly used to explain concepts, support research, and provide individualized learning assistance. Its growing presence raises questions about independent reasoning, creativity, verification, and equitable access. This exploratory cross-sectional survey examined respondents? reported AI use, perceived educational benefits, and cognitive abilities they considered important to protect. A total of 66 respondents participated in this exploratory cross-sectional survey, which combined descriptive quantitative analysis with summaries of open-ended responses. Sixty-four respondents (97.0%) reported using ChatGPT or a similar AI assistant. Personalized learning was selected as an expected benefit by 50 (75.8%), while 48 (72.7%) identified understanding difficult concepts as an AI use or benefit. Critical thinking was the most frequently selected cognitive skill to protect (55; 83.3%), followed by creativity (52; 78.8%), problem-solving (48; 72.7%), and decision-making (47; 71.2%). Reported themes included individualized explanations, convenient information access, dependence concerns, verification, equity, and teacher guidance. Based on these findings and relevant literature, the article proposes a preliminary six-principle Future Minds Framework. The small exploratory sample and self-reported data do not support generalization or causal conclusions about cognition. Further research should evaluate the framework and examine measurable learning outcomes.

documents.abstract: Accurate identification of building structural materials is a critical step in structural safety assessment and damage detection. Traditional image‑based classification methods are limited by factors such as illumination, occlusion, and surface treatment, making it difficult to effectively distinguish different materials using visual features alone. To address this problem, an intelligent recognition method for building structural materials based on multi‑modal data fusion is proposed. First, a prompting method based on a multi‑modal large language model is designed to generate structured text descriptions tailored to material classification tasks, covering discriminative information such as surface characteristics, geometric details, signs of degradation, and material inference. Second, a multi‑modal neural network named MRNet is proposed. It introduces a lightweight text feature transformer that reshapes the global vector from the Contrastive Language‑Image Pre‑training (CLIP) text encoder into a sequence and adds positional encoding. A lightweight text-feature encoder further refines the CLIP global text embedding through nonlinear transformation and channel mixing, alleviating the information compression caused by the original CLIP global pooling. The model adopts a decision‑level learnable weighted fusion strategy, where the decision results from the image and text modalities are fused through a learnable linear layer, enabling efficient cross‑modal integration without complex feature alignment. Furthermore, Bayesian optimization is introduced to automatically tune key hyperparameters such as learning rate, batch size, and weight decay coefficient. Experimental results on the PEER dataset show that MRNet achieves 96.00% in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, significantly outperforming mainstream image classification models such as AlexNet, MobileNet‑v3, ResNet, and VGG. The proposed method provides a high‑accuracy, high‑efficiency multi‑modal solution for building structural material identification.

Full-reference image quality assessment metrics such as PSNR and SSIM misalign with human perceptual judgments on texture and shape distortions, a limitation documented across multiple benchmarks. Deep perceptual metrics such as LPIPS substantially close this gap but produce opaque scores that cannot be attributed to specific image regions, a concern amplified by emerging Artificial Intelligence regulation requirements. We propose EDOKS (Earth mover’s Distance and Oklab Similarity), a white-box full-reference IQA metric that decomposes perceptual dissimilarity into two interpretable terms: a texture term, computed via Earth Mover’s Distance on Gabor filter signatures, and a chromatic term, computed as pixel-wise Euclidean distance in the Oklab perceptual color space. Evaluated on the Berkeley-Adobe Perceptual Patch Similarity dataset, which includes traditional, CNN-generated, and geometric distortions, EDOKS outperforms all tested low-level full-reference competitors on both the JND and 2AFC subsets, measured respectively by correlation with human judgments and agreement with human choices, achieving results close to deep perceptual metrics without any learned parameters. Beyond the scalar score, EDOKS produces pixel-level heatmaps that localize texture and chromatic discrepancies independently, exposing failure modes invisible to luminance-based metrics and providing users with verifiable evidence for the assigned similarity score.

Rapid technological advancement in the twenty-first century has resulted in alteration of s the relationships between humans and machines which further results in reshaping perceptions of cognition. In the current era, artificial intelligence is progressing in various domains blurring the boundaries between human and technology and reshaping the perceptions of cognition, consciousness and identity. The series Better than us explores the themes of artificial consciousness, human dependence on technology and reconfiguration of emotional and cognitive capacities. A number of studies have examined Artificial intelligence in literature, films and dramas, however limited research has explored the cognitive impacts of human dependence on artificial intelligence in the series Better Than US. Thereby using Catherin Belsey’s textual analysis model under the broader umbrella of Hayles post humanist theory the current Study aims to explore the representation of cognitive transformations in humans through artificial intelligence in the series Better Than US. The findings of the study reveal that the series Better Than Us presents artificial intelligence as a transformative force which reshapes human ethical cognition. The series transform the traditional assumption that moral judgment and authority belong exclusively to humans. The character representation of Arisa demonstrates the role of AI systems in decision making, legal interpretation, and protective actions. This results in a redistribution of ethical responsibility between humans and intelligent machine. The analysis further elucidates that human characters gradually begin to negotiate morality within technologically mediated environments where machine reasoning influences social and institutional structures. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Human-Machine relations, Posthumanism, Better Than Us.

Abstract The industrialization of the construction industry has transformed traditional practices by streamlining construction processes in controlled, factory-based environments through construction manufacturing production systems, in which building components are produced in factories and assembled on-site. Beyond improvements in efficiency and environmental performance, this production paradigm establishes long-term relationships between workers and management, creating an opportunity for human-centric construction manufacturing that prioritizes workers’ well-being as a core element of production within the Industry 5.0 paradigm. Human-centric construction manufacturing offers a practical means of integrating worker well-being, safety, mental health, inclusiveness, and skill development into construction production systems. Despite growing interest in human-centric considerations, existing research remains fragmented, loosely defined, and predominantly technology-driven. To address these gaps, this paper presents a scoping review on human-centric construction manufacturing that synthesizes key research themes, enabling technologies, emerging trends, research gaps, and future research directions within construction production systems. A total of 54 articles were included in the review, spanning three research areas examined from a human-centric perspective, i.e., ergonomics, safety, and workforce planning, each further categorized into subresearch areas. Workers’ mental health, equity, diversity, inclusion, and holistic well-being in the construction manufacturing paradigm remain significant and underexplored research opportunities. Among the most prominent technologies were simulation, virtual reality, optimization, sensing technologies, and 3D modeling, while computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and digital twins were less frequently applied, despite their strong potential to support human-centric construction manufacturing. Overall, this review establishes a comprehensive foundation for understanding the current state of human-centric construction manufacturing, identifies critical research needs, and provides guidance for future efforts toward developing safer, healthier, and more productive factory environments that support resilient construction manufacturing systems.

The rapid expansion of urban air mobility calls for safe low-altitude corridor networks across complex urban airspace, where heterogeneous positioning uncertainties caused by navigation and communication errors elevate collision risk and constrain both route feasibility and network-wide connectivity. To address this issue, this study proposes a risk-informed network planning framework that integrates three-dimensional collision risk modeling with language-model-guided multi-agent learning for the construction of safe urban air corridor networks. Specifically, a three-dimensional collision risk map is first constructed by translating navigation and communication errors into spatially varying positioning uncertainty, providing a unified safety basis for route feasibility evaluation. Network construction is then formulated as a cooperative graph connectivity task on the risk map, in which multiple learning agents jointly balance route connectivity, construction cost, and accumulated collision risk through coordinated training and distributed execution. To further accelerate convergence in complex urban environments, a vision-language model interprets airspace structure and produces high-level priors that steer agents toward safer altitude regimes. A case study over the low-altitude airspace of Nanjing demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework in producing risk-compliant air corridor networks, with language-model-derived priors further reducing training effort by 50.3 %. The results support safer and more systematic air network strategies in complex urban environments, contributing to evidence-based collision risk mitigation and airspace management in the emerging urban low-altitude economy.

The most significant problem facing software security firms in the current cybersecurity system is the fact that new strains of malware keep on appearing. The achievement of successful detection of malicious software based on both static and dynamic data remains unmet despite the further realization of different approaches to deep learning and machine learning. Defects in encryption, packaging, and distribution, the discrepancies between the distribution of malware samples in families, make this issue even worse. To do actual malware research that utilizes deep learning methods, you will require data scientists of appropriate competence, large amounts of computer power (particularly GPUs) and time. In order to overcome such issues, this approach involves a hybrid approach to feature extraction that integrates wavelet and other statistical features based on benchmarked malware image sets. A classification model based on gradient-boosting can be used reliably to classify different types of malwares. Further, this paper examined the capability of the machine learning system to Classify in-distribution test samples well. This method is properly tested on the two benchmarked datasets MelVis and MALIMG to ensure its effectiveness. By joining these two sets of data it is possible to test the suggested technique using varied array of samples. The proposed approach outperforms the state-of-the-art techniques with an incredible accuracy rate of 100% using MALIMG and 98.10 and 98.40% using combined datasets. Its value extends far beyond cybersecurity in such spheres as sustaining IoT ecosystems to assist in improving networked devices and systems.

The complexity of today's transportation networks has made road safety, accident detection, and risk management increasingly challenging. Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) offer a technological base to enhance transportation safety by incorporating sensors, communications, data processing, and intelligent decision-making. This review discusses the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for accident detection and risk prediction in ITS by examining information sources, methodologies, accident investigation, and associated challenges. It examines the use of machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, spatiotemporal modeling, and multimodal AI for accident detection, risk prediction, severity analysis, and active safety management. This review of studies suggests that collecting traffic, vehicle, road, environmental, geographical, historical, and driver-related information can improve understanding of collisions and support timely safety decisions. The review also highlights the importance of explainable and reliable AI that provides transparency, dependability, and accountability. However, the obstacles include data heterogeneity, model generalization, dynamic conditions, scalability, quick implementation, privacy considerations, security requirements, and compatible information systems. In conclusion, incorporating AI in ITS may have the power to shift road-safety management from reactive measures to data-driven approaches.

documents.abstract: Abstract Background For public health policy research, it is crucial to monitor policy debates to inform evidence-based policymaking. One popular method is to analyze the news for salient frames used to argue for or against a controversial topic. However, this method is time and resource-intensive since domain experts need to manually analyze relevant articles to identify frames. This study presents an approach for using large language models (LLMs) to extract frames and to systematically evaluate results. Methods Building on the results of a framing analysis of the German media debate about a tax on animal-based foods, we developed a systematic workflow to utilize LLMs to extract all instances of the 10 most frequent manually coded negative frames from 46 news articles. With one prompt per article in a few-shot setting we generated a list of quote/frame pairs. We then evaluated results against human-coded ones and calculated precision, recall, and F1-score. Results GPT-5 achieved 79.8% precision and 79.8% recall, identifying 75.2% of manually coded frames. Extracted quotes generally aligned with human-extracted text sections. Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview yielded higher precision but lower recall, resulting in a comparable F1-score (79.0% vs. 79.8% with GPT-5). These findings suggest the approach is generalizable across different frontier models. Conclusions This study introduces a workflow for LLM-assisted frame extraction and transparent evaluation against an expert reference standard. Integrating this approach into public health policy coding can save resources and accelerate analysis. Ultimately, this could increase the representativeness and timeliness of data, enhancing our understanding of ongoing public health policy debates.

Reconstructive plastic surgery has evolved from relatively simple techniques of wound closure and skin replacement into a multidisciplinary field capable of restoring increasingly complex anatomy and function. Skin grafts and local or regional flaps remain indispensable because they are reliable, accessible and clinically established, while microsurgery has expanded the ability to transfer vascularized tissue to defects created by trauma, burns, cancer, congenital anomalies and other conditions. At the same time, tissue engineering and regenerative medicine have introduced a different objective: rather than merely replacing missing tissue, the field increasingly seeks to recreate biological environments that support regeneration, vascularization, innervation and long-term functional integration. This narrative review examines that transition and integrates conventional reconstructive surgery with contemporary advances in biomaterials, stem-cell-based therapies, tissue-engineered skin, vascular and nerve engineering, three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting, digital surgical planning, artificial intelligence (AI), robotic microsurgery and emerging digital-twin concepts. Particular attention is given to the persistent translational barriers that separate promising laboratory demonstrations from routine clinical treatment, including vascularization, cell survival during printing, innervation, immune response, mechanical integration, long-term durability, manufacturing, cost and regulatory uncertainty. AI is examined as an enabling technology rather than a replacement for surgical judgment, with applications in virtual surgical planning, image analysis, flap-risk prediction and postoperative monitoring. Evidence summarized in the supporting research material indicates that virtual planning can improve geometric accuracy and that machine-learning systems may assist in risk stratification and monitoring, but external validation and prospective clinical evaluation remain essential. The review concludes that the most credible future is not the disappearance of conventional reconstruction but the convergence of microsurgery, regenerative biology, advanced biomaterials, computational planning, AI and biofabrication. The central trajectory of the field is therefore a shift from replacement toward regeneration, with the long-term goal of producing patient-specific tissues that are vascularized, innervated, mechanically appropriate and functionally integrated.
